1.w: “I made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I entertain thoughts against a virgin?

2.w: What then would be one’s lot from God above, one’s heritage from the Almighty on high?

3.w: Is it not misfortune for the unjust and disaster for those who work iniquity?

4.w: Does he not see my ways and count all my steps?

5.w: If I have walked in falsehood and if my foot has hastened to deceit—

6.w: let him weigh me with honest scales; then God will discover my integrity.

7.w: If my footsteps have strayed from the way, if my heart has gone after my eyes, or if anything has defiled my hands,

8.w: then let me sow and let another eat, and let my crops be uprooted.

9.w: If my heart has been enticed by a woman, and I have lain in wait at my neighbor’s door,

10.w: then let my wife turn the millstone for another man, and may other men commit adultery with her.

11.w: For I would have committed a shameful act, an iniquity to be judged.

12.w: For it is a fire that devours even to Destruction, and it would uproot all my harvest.

13.w: “If I have disregarded the right of my male servants or my female servants when they disputed with me,

14.w: then what will I do when God confronts me in judgment; when he intervenes, how will I respond to him?

15.w: Did not the one who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same one form us in the womb?

16.w: If I have refused to give the poor what they desired, or caused the eyes of the widow to fail,

17.w: if I ate my morsel of bread myself, and did not share any of it with orphans —

18.w: but from my youth I raised the orphan like a father, and from my mother’s womb I guided the widow —

19.w: if I have seen anyone about to perish for lack of clothing, or a poor man without a coat,

20.w: whose heart did not bless me as he warmed himself with the fleece of my sheep,

21.w: if I have raised my hand to vote against the orphan, when I saw my support in the court,

22.w: then let my arm fall from the shoulder, let my arm be broken off at the socket.

23.w: For the calamity from God was a terror to me, and by reason of his majesty I was powerless.

24.w: “If I have put my confidence in gold or said to pure gold, ‘You are my security!’

25.w: if I have rejoiced because of the extent of my wealth, or because of the great wealth my hand had gained,

26.w: if I looked at the sun when it was shining, and the moon advancing as a precious thing,

27.w: so that my heart was secretly enticed, and my hand threw them a kiss from my mouth,

28.w: then this also would be iniquity to be judged, for I would have been false to God above.

29.w: If I have rejoiced over the misfortune of my enemy or exulted because calamity found him—

30.w: I have not even permitted my mouth to sin by asking for his life through a curse—

31.w: if the members of my household have never said, ‘If only there were someone who has not been satisfied from Job’s meat!’—

32.w: but no stranger had to spend the night outside, for I opened my doors to the traveler —

33.w: if I have covered my transgressions as men do, by hiding iniquity in my heart,

34.w: because I was terrified of the great multitude, and the contempt of families terrified me, so that I remained silent and would not go outdoors—

35.w: “If only I had someone to hear me! Here is my signature — let the Almighty answer me! If only I had an indictment that my accuser had written.

36.w: Surely I would wear it proudly on my shoulder, I would bind it on me like a crown;

37.w: I would give him an accounting of my steps; like a prince I would draw near to him.

38.w: “If my land cried out against me and all its furrows wept together,

39.w: if I have eaten its produce without paying, or caused the death of its owners,

40.w: then let thorns sprout up in place of wheat, and in place of barley, noxious weeds.” The words of Job are ended.
